name: Cinch
description: Cinch is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

history.origins: American trick-taking game of the all fours family; developed in Denver, Colorado in the 1880s. Evolved from Auction Pitch via Pedro. Points are awarded for winning tricks containing certain cards (Game point for trump Ten, five each for Right and Left Pedro). Played to a target such as 42 or 51 points.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

rules.objective: Be the first player to achieve the winning condition through strategic play of cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. Setup: prepare players, deck or tiles, and opening layout according to the variant. 2. Turn loop: each player performs one legal action (play, capture, build, bet, or pass/draw as applicable). 3. Resolution: each action updates control of tricks/cards/pot/layout. 4. End condition: when hand-ending criteria are met, scoring is computed and match state advances.
keyRules: Play proceeds in turn order with only legal actions allowed.
Round resolution follows the variant's scoring and bonus conditions.
Match winner is determined by agreed target score or elimination condition.

strategy.basic: Cinch: follow rules; strategy depends on variant.
strategy.intermediate: Track revealed information (cards, tiles, tricks, or betting patterns) and adjust plan as opponent ranges narrow.
strategy.advanced: Use tempo and denial lines to convert small positional edges into scoring swings in late hand phases.
tips: Fix the exact local variant before play so edge cases are predictable.
Plan two turns ahead: most mistakes come from giving opponents forced value.
Recalculate risk near end-of-hand scoring thresholds.
